title: Integrate PR #457 review follow-ups (curse doff gate + stable-recovery correctness)
description:
Integration parent for the four PR #457 post-merge review follow-ups:

- eshyra-gacz (P1): Demon Armor stays permanently undoffable after its curse ends
- eshyra-q93i (P1): Migration 0020 strands pre-existing stable-at-zero characters
- eshyra-r2ps (P1): advanceWorldTime clock commit and stable-recovery resolution not atomic
- eshyra-cc3c (P2): Rest completion omits stableRecoveries from benefits/persisted evidence

See those beads for full defect analysis with file/line references. The review recommends one follow-up PR covering all four, with the first three treated as re-freeze blockers.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Doff of a blocksDoff cursed item is gated on the applicable *live* curse state, not the static flag: don Demon Armor → doff fails → remove curse condition → doff succeeds → item still held, not_worn. No don-onset state definition ⇒ keep failing closed. Ambiguous wear state ⇒ keep failing closed.
2. Legacy stable-at-zero characters (schedule columns NULL) get a deterministic, documented adoption via a NEW migration (0020 is immutable), and resolveStableRecoveries throws on a stable-at-zero row with missing or partially populated schedule fields instead of silently skipping.
3. All due stable recoveries resolve inside the same withTransaction callback as the clock transition in advanceWorldTime; an injected failure during recovery rolls back the clock advance.
4. complete() includes stableRecoveries in the benefits object (tool response AND persisted benefits_json), with tests for both.
5. npm run verify:worktree passes on the integration branch; no weakened existing tests.

## Integration plan

Work lands via child dispatch branches merged into branch eshyra-<this-bead>; single PR to main from this branch. Close the four defect beads when the PR merges.
